x: Great improvement has been shown by Bob Barnes, and he should do well in the coming season. Johnny Morris and Malcolm Byard have also made great strides forward. It is a pity that Malcolm has soon to return to Sheffield.
Fotheringham was maintaining a short lead over Cyril Yescombe and Johnny Morris, and a little further back still, Bert East had his eyes set on catching George Checkley and another handicap award!
Dave King started steadily, mindful of his retirement last year, with Johnny Morris John Keown and Bernard Eglinton packing well a little further back.

Support from other Belgravians was fantastic, Captain Ray Hall, Charlie MacLennan, Carl Lawton, Brian Ward, Johnny Morris, Steve Brown, The Wilson brothers as well as many others all played a part on this hot day.
George Beecham also suffered a bit but those two stalwarts Johnny Morris and John Keown kept us in the reckoning by helping the others through - truly great team men.
A specially arranged sharpener before the National '10' gave Tommy Cook the opportunity to romp away with the prize closely pursued by Johnny Morris and John Keown.
Carl Lawton made an emergency stop in Croydon to pick up 2p on the road, taking great care that Johnny Morris, this time in the attendants seat on a bicycle, was not there first.

Johnny Morris and John Keown could not decide as to which of them was the most unfit. The appearance of Eric Stroud could bring a bit of depth to our long distance side as could Paul Wiltshire to our sprint team.
The reliable Dave King, John Keown and Johnny Morris finished but with no Lawton, Middleton, Moullin, Duquemin or Duncan, their efforts were in vain.
…nda, wanting to do everybody's job and absent for lunch (about 4 minutes - she couldn't stay away from all that money), Johnny Morris and son and the man of the year Ray Hall.…

Leading the table of 'Brightons' successfully completed since the last war are John Keown with 16 (consecutive); George Beecham with 15; Joe Wilson, Harry Shields and Bernard Eglington with 12 each; Gordon Doubleday with 11 (2 before the war) and Johnny Morris and Dave King with 10 each.

It was an oversight in the last issue of the 'Belgravian' that no mention was made of Johnny Morris, John Keown and Eric Stroud, all of whom competed in the notorious 'Brighton' and hence doubled our number of finishers of the year before.
The team consisted of four walkers; George Beecham, Dave King, Johnny Morris and John Keown. For George and Dave it was their first attempt at 100 miles.
Fotheringham was 11th with 5:44 and Johnny Morris 19th with 5:54:07.

Carl again proved to be the winner, this time with 13:23, with Richard Tanner and Johnny Morris filling the other medal positions. Peter Morris took the Youths 2Km. in 11.08.

To Ted Weldin for also helping with the field events as did Johnny Morris, Colin Pearson and Bill Merryman. Thanks to Gordon Doubleday and Derek Crookes for time keeping and Bill Lucas for track judging.
